notes: A STIB day pass costs 8 EUR, and the city centre is walkable. Take the train to Bruges and Ghent (weekend tickets are 50% off). The train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes.

In December there is a light show on Grand-Place and a Christmas market (Plaisirs d'Hiver). Winter weather is 3-7°C and rainy, so museums and beer bars are warm refuges. The Laeken greenhouses open in April and May.
Waffles cost 3-7 EUR (Brussels = rectangular and light, Liège = dense and sugary), frites 4-6, moules-frites 25, beer 4-6. For a tip, round up the bill.
French is spoken in Brussels and Flemish in Bruges and Ghent; English also works. Avoid the restaurants on Rue des Bouchers (tourist traps), except Chez Léon.
Museums are closed on Mondays. Book Atomium and Belfry tickets online. On the first Wednesday of the month, many museums are free in the afternoon.
Chocolate: Neuhaus, Marcolini, Wittamer, Mary. Leonidas is cheap and good.

stops.name: Grand-Place
stops.tips: A UNESCO square with guildhouses and the Town Hall, empty before 10:00. Manneken Pis is 2 streets away. In even-numbered years the Flower Carpet appears in August.

stops.name: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
stops.tips: A glass-roofed arcade from 1847, home to Neuhaus's first shop and Pierre Marcolini.

stops.name: Maison Dandoy Grand-Place
stops.tips: Speculoos and Brussels waffles (rectangular, light) since 1829. Compare with a Liège waffle (dense, sugary).

stops.name: Fritland
stops.tips: A friterie next to the square. Try the twice-fried chips and a mitraillette sandwich, part of UNESCO-recognised culture.

stops.name: Delirium Café
stops.tips: Guinness record holder with 2,000+ beers. In Impasse de la Fidélité, opposite Jeanneke Pis.

backups.name: Chez Léon
backups.tips: Moules-frites (mussels and chips) since 1893. On Rue des Bouchers.

backups.name: Museum of the City of Brussels Maison du Roi
backups.tips: The city museum in the King's House on the square, with Manneken Pis costumes.

stops.name: Magritte Museum
stops.tips: 200+ surrealist works (bowler hat, apple). Combined ticket with the Royal Museums 15 EUR, closed Mondays.

stops.name: Place du Grand Sablon
stops.tips: Antique dealers and chocolatiers (Wittamer, Marcolini), plus an antiques market at weekends.

stops.name: Le Pain Quotidien Sablon
stops.tips: The chain's first branch. Try the tartines and soup.

stops.name: Place du Jeu de Balle Flea Market
stops.tips: A daily flea market in Marolles, best in the morning, in Brueghel's old neighbourhood.

stops.name: Musical Instruments Museum MIM
stops.tips: An Art Nouveau building (the Old England store). Instruments come with headphones, and the rooftop café has views.

backups.name: Wittamer Sablon
backups.tips: A pastry shop from 1910 and royal supplier.

backups.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
backups.tips: Bruegel and Rubens. Go instead of the MIM (combined ticket with Magritte).

stops.name: Markt Bruges
stops.tips: Take the train, 1 hour from Brussels-Midi (~15 EUR). The square has the Belfry and guildhouses.

stops.name: Belfry of Bruges
stops.tips: 366 steps to the bell chamber and a panorama over the canal town. Timed tickets.

stops.name: Bruges Canal Boat Tour
stops.tips: A 30-minute boat ride past Rozenhoedkaai (the most photographed corner). 5 departure docks.

stops.name: De Halve Maan Brewery
stops.tips: Home of Brugse Zot beer. The tour takes 45 minutes plus a beer, with rooftop views. Go at lunchtime.

stops.name: Begijnhof Bruges
stops.tips: A beguine courtyard from 1245, very peaceful. Minnewater, the Lake of Love, is nearby.

backups.name: Frituur Bruges Markt
backups.tips: Two chip huts beneath the Belfry.

backups.name: Groeningemuseum
backups.tips: Flemish Primitives (van Eyck). Go instead of the Begijnhof.

stops.name: Atomium
stops.tips: The 102 m iron crystal from Expo 1958. Spheres and views, book online (combined ticket with Design Museum).

stops.name: Mini-Europe
stops.tips: 350 miniatures of Europe's landmarks, at the foot of the Atomium. Good with children.

stops.name: Atomium Restaurant
stops.tips: A restaurant with views in the top sphere. Go to the outdoor café instead.

stops.name: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken
stops.tips: Open for only 3 weeks in April and May. At other times, see Laeken Park and the Japanese Tower from outside.

stops.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
stops.tips: A triumphal arch and museums, in the EU quarter.

backups.name: Frit Flagey
backups.tips: The city's best friterie (Place Flagey). Take the tram.

backups.name: Autoworld Cinquantenaire
backups.tips: 300 classic cars. Go instead of the park.

stops.name: Gravensteen
stops.tips: 35 minutes by train. The counts' castle has a funny audio guide and ramparts with city views.

stops.name: Graslei & Korenlei
stops.tips: Guildhouses along the canal, the best view in Ghent from St Michael's Bridge.

stops.name: Saint Bavo's Cathedral Ghent Altarpiece
stops.tips: Van Eyck's Adoration of the Mystic Lamb panel (AR tour). Opposite the Belfry.

stops.name: Patershol
stops.tips: A medieval quarter full of restaurants. Try Gentse waterzooi (chicken stew).

stops.name: Ghent Canal Boat Tour
stops.tips: 40 minutes, departing from Graslei. Then take the train back.

backups.name: Belfry of Ghent
backups.tips: A UNESCO bell tower. Go instead of the cathedral.

days.theme: Ixelles, Art Nouveau and the EU

stops.name: Horta Museum
stops.tips: The home of Victor Horta, the inventor of Art Nouveau, in Saint-Gilles. Timed tickets, closed Mondays.

stops.name: Avenue Louise Art Nouveau Walk
stops.tips: The façades of Hôtel Tassel and Solvay, in Ixelles.

stops.name: Place Flagey & Ixelles Ponds
stops.tips: A square and lakeside, with a market at weekends.

stops.name: Belga Café Flagey
stops.tips: A café on Place Flagey. Order a croque and a beer, opposite Frit Flagey.

stops.name: European Parliament Parlamentarium
stops.tips: A free interactive EU museum. Hemicycle tour with your passport.

backups.name: Moeder Lambic Fontainas
backups.tips: A bar for lambic and gueuze beers. A more local option than Delirium.

backups.name: Museum of Natural Sciences
backups.tips: Europe's largest dinosaur hall. Go instead of the Parlamentarium.

stops.name: Choco-Story Brussels
stops.tips: A chocolate museum with demonstrations, next to Grand-Place.

stops.name: Pierre Marcolini Grand Sablon
stops.tips: One of Belgium's best chocolatiers. Buy a gift box.

stops.name: Noordzee Mer du Nord
stops.tips: A stand-up fish bar in Sainte-Catherine. Have shrimp croquettes and white wine as a farewell.

stops.name: Gare Centrale
stops.tips: The train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes (Midi/Central). The bus to Charleroi takes 1 hour. Farewell.

backups.name: Comics Art Museum
backups.tips: Tintin and the Smurfs, in a Horta building. Go instead of the chocolate.
